newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X set up US$5 mln legal fund last year - report.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X set up US$5 mln legal fund last year - report.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd, facing a spate of lawsuits after the Busang gold scandal, created a US$5 million trust fund late last year to pay the legal costs of the company's officers and directors, a report made public this week showed.

In its report filed with a Canadian court, Price Waterhouse Ltd, which is monitoring the gold prospector's accounts, said the "indemnity fund" was set up last December with an offshore trustee. Under the arrangement, "those funds are held for the benefit of, and are security for, Bre-X's indemnity of its officers and directors," the report said.

Bre-X and its officers and directors face at least 11 lawsuits filed by Canadian and U.S. shareholders after the company's Busang gold play in Indonesia -- once touted as the biggest find this century -- was deemed in early May to be an unprecedented fraud.

Price Waterhouse, appointed monitor of Bre-X and its sister companies when they received creditor protection last month, said the unnamed trustee told Bre-X that it froze payments on indemnity claims.

Before Price Waterhouse was appointed under Canada's Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act, Bre-X paid US$700,000 to lawyers representing seven officers and directors as an advance on payments from the fund -- US$100,000 for each company official, the report said.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Bre-X and sister firms Bresea Resources Ltd and Bro-X Minerals Ltd had C$35.9 million in cash at the end of May, according to the Price Waterhouse report. The firms also had C$38.6 million in working capital at May 31.

The report also revealed that Bresea lent Arm-X Minerals -- a little known private firm among several associated with Bre-X Chairman David Walsh -- C$500,000 in January 1997 as seed money for a planned public offering.
But ownership of Arm-X was recently transferred to a relative of Walsh and the loan had not been repaid, Price Waterhouse said.
Walsh is chairman of of Bre-X, Bresea and Bro-X. Cease-trade orders have been slapped on the shares of all three.
